## Executive Summary: The 2026 BOJ Pivot and the End of Free Funding

## 1. Problem Statement

The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) 2026 interest-rate normalization—projected cumulative hikes toward **≈1.00%** from the effective zero bound—represents the structural termination of the global yen carry trade's "free funding" era. Since the 2008 crisis, the yen carry trade has functioned as a global liquidity pipeline: institutional and retail investors borrowed JPY at ~0% policy rates, converted proceeds into high-yield emerging-market (EM) currencies (TRY, EGP, PKR) or duration-sensitive US technology equities, and harvested the positive interest differential. The BOJ has explicitly signaled upside inflation risks and a hawkish pivot as early as September 2024 [10], following suspected yen-buying interventions in New York markets. The transmission chain—**BOJ hike → JPY appreciation → margin calls on JPY-funded positions → forced deleveraging → cross-asset contagion**—now threatens to propagate through two vulnerable receptor classes: (i) reserve-constrained, dollar-denominated-debt EM economies, and (ii) leveraged US tech equity portfolios. This report models the 2026 scenario's macro-financial impact, quantifies contagion risk using duration-distribution and leverage-amplifier frameworks [3][1], and delivers actionable policy and portfolio recommendations.
